A performance release. Claude Buddy's idle CPU on macOS drops from about 37%, and it stops streaming about 100 MB a minute to its remote-control peers. Animations also run at their proper speed for the first time.

## Fixed

- **Animated persona pictures, pulses and hover timers now run on time.** Every timer in Buddy had been firing about 100–200 ms late since the UI thread started being claimed before the native platform was up: the dispatcher kept the clock it was created with, while the platform scheduled timers against a later one. An animated persona that should play at 25 fps showed about 4. Timers now run on the platform's clock. Pulses and the danger-ring breath are capped at 10 fps, and idle orbs breathe at 5, so the extra accuracy doesn't cost CPU.
- **Idle CPU on macOS is much lower.** It was about 37%; it's about 9% with three animated personas and networked features off, and 15–19% with everything on. A usage ring in the danger band "breathes", and that breathing was an animation that never ended, so the app redrew on every screen refresh for as long as the ring stayed there. It now breathes on a 20 fps timer. It looks the same, but costs a fraction of the work.
- **Remote-control peers no longer stream megabytes every 10 seconds.** Each peer poll resent every persona picture in full, so 11–15 MB animated GIFs went out every 10 s to each peer, about 106 MB a minute. Now a roster that hasn't changed gets a short "unchanged" reply, and persona pictures are sent once and then referred to by fingerprint. Peers running an older build still work, at the old cost, until they're updated.
- **A Mac that stays locked no longer loses Buddy after 12 hours.** On a headless or always-locked Mac, Buddy waited 12 hours for an unlock, then tried to start its window anyway and crashed. Now it keeps serving its peers for as long as the screen is locked, and starts its window only when an unlock actually happens.
- **Fewer `claude agents --json` launches.** Buddy now asks only the Claude Code accounts that have a session on screen, and still asks every account whenever a session can't be traced to one.
- **Hidden orbs no longer keep animating.** With orbs turned off, animated persona pictures stop and pick up again from the same frame when the orbs come back.
- **The Windows installer no longer exits with an error on a per-user install.** The firewall step needs admin rights, so it now runs only on an administrative install.

## Known limitations

- A per-user Windows install adds no firewall rule for the peer link, because that needs admin rights. Windows asks the first time Buddy listens.
- The remaining ~10% idle CPU on macOS hasn't been investigated yet.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.9-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.9-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.5.9-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

## Upgrading

Replace the app as usual. **On macOS, if you re-install you have to re-grant the Automation and Local Network permissions.** Replacing `/Applications/Claude Buddy.app` gives the app a new code identity, and macOS doesn't carry those permissions over to it. Without Automation, click-to-focus stops working; without Local Network, anything on your LAN, such as an OpenClaw gateway or a remote-control peer, can't be reached. Re-grant both in System Settings → Privacy & Security.
